---
# ============================================================================
# ERN home page. Edit the copy here, then rebuild:
#
#     quarto render index.qmd
#
# That overwrites index.html in place. git is the safety net — review
# `git diff index.html` before committing.
#
# The page chrome lives in _extensions/ern/home/template.html. Everything a
# person normally wants to change (headings, blurbs, cards, links, footer)
# is a field below, so the template should rarely need touching.
#
# NOTE: Quarto parses these values as Markdown with smart typography on, so a
# bare apostrophe becomes a curly one. Write &#39; to keep it straight, which
# is what the rest of the site uses. Do not backslash-escape: inside a folded
# block scalar (>-) YAML keeps the backslash and it lands on the page.
# Colons and URLs need no escaping.
#
# The two maps under maps/ carry their own copy and their own data. The
# coverage map's roster is generated — see code/build_home_map_data.py.
# ============================================================================

title: "Eviction Research Network — eviction data across the US"

  canonical: "https://evictionresearch.net/"
  author: "Eviction Research Network, UC Berkeley"
  og_title: "Eviction Research Network — UC Berkeley"
  og_image: "https://evictionresearch.net/images/ern_logo/1Av2/EvictionStudy_logo_v09_1A_LOGO_BANNER.png"
  description: >-
    The Eviction Research Network at UC Berkeley collects eviction court
    records and turns them into maps, state profiles, and trends that show
    where evictions happen, who they fall on, and how they change over time.
    It is the home of the Housing Precarity Risk Model (HPRM).
  short_description: >-
    Eviction data, displacement research, and the Housing Precarity Risk Model
    from UC Berkeley&#39;s Eviction Research Network.
  keywords: >-
    eviction research, housing precarity, displacement, gentrification,
    eviction data, housing policy, Housing Precarity Risk Model, HPRM,
    UC Berkeley, Department of Sociology

atlas:
  h1_lead: "Eviction data across the"
  h1_em: "US."
  lede: >-
    This map is a census of where eviction data resides. States in red have
    an ERN analysis.
  badge: "Under development"
  note: >-
    We add states and sources as we verify them.
  # Counts are printed by code/build_home_map_data.py on every run. Rerun it
  # after the directory changes and bring these into line. The 5 counts states
  # with no statewide public source (AL, IA, KS, MS, SD), the same five as the
  # Directory. State of Eviction Data counts a narrower set, the 3 with no
  # public data from any source (AL, IA, SD). Keep the word "statewide".
  meta: >-
    Last updated <strong>November 2026</strong> · 50 states and D.C. ·
    <strong>8</strong> with an ERN profile, <strong>5</strong> with no
    statewide public source.
  button:
    label: "See every state&#39;s data →"
    href: "eviction-data-atlas.html"
  map:
    src: "maps/us-coverage-map.html"
    title: "Eviction data across the US — select a state"
    height: 800

hprm:
  h2_lead: "The Housing Precarity"
  h2_em: "Risk Model."
  sub: >-
    HPRM 2.0 scores census tracts across the contiguous United States for
    eviction risk and market displacement risk on one 0 to 8 scale.
  button:
    label: "Explore the model →"
    href: "https://evictionresearch.net/hprm/"
  # The raster inside this map is rendered for the width this column gives it.
  # Widen the column and the tract marks need re-tuning — see
  # code/render_hprm_national.mjs.
  map:
    src: "maps/us-hprm-map.html"
    title: "HPRM 2.0 national risk map"
    height: 520

research:
  h2_lead: "Our"
  h2_em: "research."
  more_label: "Read more →"
  button:
    label: "All research →"
    href: "research.html"
  cards:
    - kicker: "Working paper · 2026"
      title: >-
        Keeping People in Their Homes: the impact of emergency rental
        assistance on evictions
      body: >-
        This neighborhood-level study tests whether $46.6 billion in emergency
        rental assistance reduced eviction filings. It covers 700+ counties
        and 12,000+ census tracts in 22 states.
      href: "https://evictionresearch.net/hud-era/"
    - kicker: "State profile · 2026"
      title: "Washington eviction filings, 2016–2026"
      body: >-
        Over the past 38 months, 1 in 44 renter households faced an eviction
        filing. That is roughly 52% above the pre-pandemic normal. Nine of 39
        counties exceed the state rate.
      href: "https://evictionresearch.net/washington/"
    - kicker: "Cityscape (HUD) · 2024"
      title: >-
        Toward a national eviction data collection strategy using natural
        language processing
      body: >-
        ERN read 111,740 Washington eviction court records from scanned PDF
        and TIFF images. It then estimated the racial and gender disparities
        in filings that county-level counts do not show.
      href: "cityscape-2024.html"

mission:
  eyebrow: "Research for social good"
  h2_lead: "What we"
  h2_em: "do."
  # Revised 2026-11-05 at Tim's direction from the client-supplied ERN
  # description (prose review H5, 2026-11-02), in the plain register.
  paragraphs:
    - >-
      The Eviction Research Network collects, analyzes, and maps eviction data
      and helps other researchers do the same. We use social and data science
      to measure racial and gender disparities in eviction, and urban theory
      to explain them.
    - >-
      We study how common eviction is and what drives it in regions with
      little research. We point readers to other scholars&#39; work. We give
      legislatures, practitioners, and advocates evidence they can use.

# Each image is a drawn SVG in images/tools/ holding synthetic values only.
# Keep it that way: no real case, name, or address on this page.
tools:
  eyebrow: "Free and open source"
  h2_lead: "Our"
  h2_em: "tools."
  intro: >-
    Eviction records sit in thousands of separate court systems, and few of
    the organizations that need them can afford to build software to read
    them. ERN releases the tools behind its research as free, open-source
    code. Courts, legal aid groups, agencies, and other researchers can use
    them to collect and analyze eviction data themselves. Anyone can read
    the code to see how our numbers are made.
  more_label: "View on GitHub →"
  cards:
    - kicker: "Python and R · AGPL-3.0"
      title: "extract-text"
      badge: "Under development"
      body: >-
        extract-text turns eviction court filings, including scanned and
        handwritten pages, into a table of cases with party names, addresses,
        and case details. It runs entirely on your own computer, so records
        never leave your hands. It was validated on more than a million pages
        of Washington State filings.
      image: "images/tools/extract-text.svg"
      alt: >-
        A scanned court summons with a handwritten address, an arrow, and
        the same case as rows of digital text.
      href: "https://evictionresearch.net/extract-text/"
      more: "Visit the site →"
    - kicker: "R package · MIT"
      title: "neighborhood"
      body: >-
        The neighborhood package holds R functions for studying neighborhood
        change with census data. They include racial typologies of census
        tracts, housing affordability by income level, and the interactive
        maps and charts used in ERN&#39;s state eviction profiles.
      image: "images/tools/neighborhood.svg"
      alt: >-
        A table of census figures, an arrow, and a map of census tracts
        shaded from light to dark blue.
      href: "https://github.com/evictionresearch/neighborhood"

# A film ERN recommends; ERN did not make it. Facts checked 2026-11-05 against
# the producer's pages (counterstoriesproductions.com/films.html,
# /screenings.html), pcusa.org/evicting, and the PCUSA news item of
# 2026-05-08 (runtime). The trailer is Vimeo 1061006434; dnt=1 asks Vimeo
# not to track visitors.
film:
  eyebrow: "For groups and classes"
  h2_lead: "Evicting the American"
  h2_em: "Dream."
  kicker: "Documentary · 2025 · 51 minutes"
  video: "https://player.vimeo.com/video/1061006434?dnt=1"
  video_title: "Trailer for Evicting the American Dream"
  paragraphs:
    - >-
      Evicting the American Dream tells the stories of children and families
      facing eviction and homelessness. The filmmakers also interview
      pediatric psychologists, social workers, tenant advocates, housing
      officials, and eviction lawyers. The film traces the causes of eviction
      and argues that eviction can be prevented.
    - >-
      Counter Stories Productions, the film arm of Presbyterian Disaster
      Assistance, made the film. The producers make it available to schools,
      organizations, and communities that want to host a screening. They also
      publish a resource guide for the discussion afterward.
  primary:
    label: "Watch on Prime Video →"
    href: "https://www.amazon.com/Evicting-American-Dream-David-Barnhart/dp/B0FSKZFKDT"
  secondary:
    label: "Host a screening →"
    href: "https://counterstoriesproductions.com/screenings.html"
  guide:
    label: "Resource guide →"
    href: "https://pcusa.org/resource/evicting-american-dream-resource-guide"

partner:
  eyebrow: "Partner with ERN"
  heading: "Working on eviction where the data is thin?"
  body: >-
    We work with courts, legal aid organizations, agencies, advocates, and
    universities. We collect and analyze court records, build data pipelines,
    train collaborators, and co-author research. If you have records no one
    has analyzed, or need help with the ones you have, get in touch.
  primary:
    label: "Start a conversation →"
    href: "mailto:evictions@berkeley.edu?Subject=Partnership%20inquiry%20via%20ERN%20website"
  secondary:
    label: "See how we work →"
    href: "methodology.html"
